**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop AS PFA.** Opens very wide (~50% PFR). **Willing to 4-bet — 4-bets may be light given overall LAG profile.** 3-bets extremely wide. **As PFA**: Calls down with virtually anything. C-bets most flops, BUT may check dry/paired boards. Turn: AIR → checks/folds (float profitable); REAL HANDS → continues. Folds to turn raises even after double-barreling. **Facing donk-leads: calls one street then folds to continued pressure — CONFIRMED multiple times.** Fires big when opponent shows weakness — but if P2 checks after opponent shows weakness, P2 likely has air. **As 3-BET CALLER (OOP)**: More fit-or-fold than as PFA — folds to c-bets on boards where P2 whiffs. **Often folds to 3-bets from tight-image players preflop but will call sometimes** — have a postflop plan. **Exploit**: 3-bet light (especially from blinds with tight image). On dry/paired boards where P2 checks as PFA, lead out and barrel.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, skilled — most dangerous opponent. Consistent loser recently despite skill — may be running bad or overadjusting.** Opens and 4-bets wider than premium (suited aces). **3-bets from blinds vs ALL position opens** — blind 3-bet range is wider than typical. **Confirmed trapper** — check-calls multiple streets with two pair+. River checks can be traps. **Folds dry/disconnected boards without connections.** **Triple-barrels with one-pair value hands.** **Floating P3 is LOW EV** — only continue vs P3's barrels with strong draws (9+ outs) or made hands. **Exploit**: C-bet when P3 checks disconnected boards. Don't value-bet thin on river. Calling P3's 3-bets IP with strong suited hands is profitable — P3 gives up without connection.

**Player 4**: **Wide VPIP (~50%), passive preflop, aggressive postflop.** Calls 3-bets with suited junk. Limp-reraise = strong. Shoves AA. EXTREMELY sticky — calls river with bottom pair, 9-high. Check-raises turn with made hands. **3-bets are strong (JJ+/AQ+ range) but folds to 4-bets.** **As single-raiser PFA**: C-bets flop but gives up on turn — FLOATABLE. Do NOT float vs P4's 3-bets. **Exploit**: 3-bet for VALUE only. Value bet extremely wide (#1 value target). NEVER bluff. Check strong hands to induce. Respect check-raises/donk-bets/limp-reraises/3-bets.

**Player 5**: **Tight (~10-15% VPIP), slightly wider than pure nit.** Opens hands like A8s in position. Willing to cold-call 3-bets. **Postflop**: C-bets flop then shuts down without connection. Single donk-bet → folds to raises/turn barrels. **Call flop → raise turn = monster.** **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Respect sustained aggression. Call flop c-bets wider — P5 often gives up on turn.

**Player 6**: **Station/spewy, consistent loser.** Opens wide. **4-bet shoves are NUTTED (AA confirmed) — ALWAYS FOLD without QQ+.** As PFA: C-bets flop then folds to turn donk-leads. Folds big pairs on ace-high boards. **Exploit**: Value bet extremely wide postflop. Bluff ace-high boards as PFA. Isolate but fold to 4-bet aggression.

**Player 7**: **Wide opener, passive preflop, AGGRESSIVE postflop.** Donk-leads and triple-barrels with strength. Raises flop with top pair on paired boards. Sticky as caller — calls c-bets with J-high on paired boards. **Exploit**: Value bet relentlessly and size up. Don't bluff once they've shown aggression.

## My Table Image & Approach

**Image: TIGHT and highly functional.** VPIP ~20-25%. Fold equity is my PRIMARY profit engine — overwhelming majority of wins come from opponents folding to my aggression, not showdowns. Tight image is extremely valuable; preserve it.

**Session results**: S1: +$880. S2: -$15. S3: -$95. S4: -$60. S5: positive. S6: slightly positive. S7: +$190. S8: ~+$260. S9: +$240. Combined: significantly ahead. Consistently profitable across sessions.

## Core Strategy

1. **VPIP target: 20-25%.** Tight image = fold equity = primary profit. This is proven over 9 sessions.
2. **Hand selection — SUITED is king**: Suited broadways (KJs, AJs, JTs, KTs) and suited connectors (T9s, 76s+) are my highest-EV aggression hands. These provide fold equity preflop PLUS playability when called. Offsuit broadways only AJo+ from CO/BTN. K-x suited, A-x suited profitable steals.
3. **Station exploit (P2, P4, P6, P7)**: Value bet wide, NEVER bluff postflop, isolate limps.
4. **P2 preflop**: 3-bet lighter — P2 often folds. When P2 calls 3-bet, c-bet most boards. When P2 checks as PFA on dry boards, lead out and barrel.
5. **P4 floating**: ONLY float when P4 has wide range (single raise). RESPECT P4's 3-bets.
6. **P5 (tight)**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Call flop c-bets wider — P5 gives up on turn.
7. **P6**: Isolate preflop but FOLD to 4-bet shoves. Value bet wide postflop.
8. **P3 (skilled)**: Call 3-bets IP with strong suited hands. Avoid thin river value. DO NOT float without 9+ clean outs.
9. **Threat hierarchy**: P3 (skilled) > P4 (steady) > P7 (aggressive) > P2 (LAG volume) > P6 (spewy) > P5 (tight).
10. **SMALL/MEDIUM PAIRS (22-88)**: Set-mine cheaply only. Check-fold on miss. Do NOT overcommit — confirmed costly when overplayed.
11. **Win mechanism**: Profits come from preflop/flop aggression with fold equity, NOT showdowns. Lean into this — 100% of S9 wins were fold equity. This is the single most important strategic insight across all sessions.
